title: fix(gateway): explain unavailable operator restart recovery
body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a restart, operator runs whose recovery source was unavailable refuse to resume without recording which capture condition caused the missing source. Operators cannot distinguish the affected client classes.

## User Impact

The existing `Skipped restart resume` JSON payload now includes `operatorRecoveryUnavailableReason`. **Diagnostics only; no authorization change.** Capture/restore eligibility, assertion ordering, refusal Error type/message, and the user-facing notice remain unchanged. Only closed reason codes are persisted; no credentials or identities are added. No database/protocol version change or migration is required. Legacy `{kind:"unavailable"}` markers still decode and produce the same refusal.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot producer previously returned only `undefined` for remote ingress without a recovery source (`src/gateway/operator-run-recovery-source.ts:87`), unauthenticated/synthetic clients (`:129`), missing auth method (`:132`), missing grant (`:135`), device connections without token identity (`:140`), shared auth without a generation (`:146`), and unsnapshotable model policy (`:93`, `:150`). Normalization could also fail (`:120`, `:182`). The queued-source producer collapsed channel model policy, missing source, and decode failures (`:45`, `:58`, `:66`).

Those existing branches now record the requested closed reason codes, unchanged in name. Snapshot failure metadata passes through the admitted authority into optional `unavailable.reason` on the existing persisted marker. The failure reporter reads that marker from the entry it already receives, keeping the diagnostic at its existing owner without an extra coordinator argument. The final change touches nine files and adds no logger, event family, state owner, or compatibility path. Production is +61/-26 lines, tests +107/-2, and lint configuration +7/-0.

The file-specific lint maximum for `operator-run-recovery.test.ts` is raised from 1,000 to exactly 1,046 nonblank, noncomment lines so the capture and legacy regressions reuse its existing fixtures. The PR test-line budget stays unchanged: +105 net lines within 400. No production lint limit was raised.

## Evidence

Red on original production source: the capture regression expects `reason: "no-auth-method"` but receives only `{kind:"unavailable"}`; the legacy decode/refusal test passes (1 failed, 1 passed, 40 skipped). Green capture proof covers three representative unavailable conditions, valid live authority, persisted JSON/decode, and the same restoration Error/message. Restart admission proof checks the new structured field and exact unchanged saved notice.

Final head `53fca7c14b4e42a9f897a4ddb04fc4a8cdc2cc1e`: **94 tests passed across all seven touched/restart-resume suites**, including the isolated-Gateway workspace and upgrade lanes. An additional 23 tests of unchanged channel/policy recovery and admitted authority inputs passed in the earlier scoped proof. Targeted gateway-root tsgo, all changed-file oxlint/format, the +105 test-line ratchet, and diff checks pass. The branch incorporates main's retired queued-input marker fields, and the new fixture uses the current marker shape.

Fresh Codex autoreview, P0–P2, against `14b9fc3c8d9454b89b9ff402ce31e39b75e41dfb` returned **scoped-clean**, with no accepted/actionable findings. A prior INDEX-only fixture finding was resolved before the final review. The final reviewed tree was committed unchanged.

The earlier CI attempt [44225333441](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44225333441) failed two pre-existing Workshop-learning cases (oversized review request and missing Learned notice). Both reproduce on original production source, and their seven relevant source inputs are identical through this branch's new main base. The earlier native merge stopped before dispatch when GitHub mergeability changed to UNKNOWN; no merge request or retained outcome existed. The current head has its own completed PR CI; no CI rerun-for-green was requested. Runtime proof uses synthetic local state; no production Gateway or server was accessed.

Current-head CI [44234033503, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44234033503) completed **failed**, with four inherited failures across two jobs. The two Workshop cases retain the same signatures and unchanged relevant inputs. Two delegated-participant-custody cases also fail: CI merged main `4a44f2031e866e7ee430d01ece41340cefddac5e`, whose child-owner inheritance now chooses the verified requester while these cases retain the prior agent-owner expectation. Both cases pass on this reviewed branch base and reproduce as failures on the exact CI baseline production source with this PR's production changes removed. The diagnostic patch was restored and the checkout is clean. Immutable preflight checkout `59cc755398166f1b7feb1e6c00409fb490aba3f3` has ordered parents (that main base, this PR head), matches the derived merge tree, and preserves all inspected failure inputs. `security-fast` passed. Native inherited-failure admission retains the failed status and independently enforces security, review, policy and writer gates.
